subject.title: Npm-valid package scopes with dots/underscores cannot map to ClawHub publishers

question: Should ClawHub accept the shipped policy that publisher handles are npm-scope-compatible identities allowing dots and underscores for exact package-scope ownership?
rationale: The code and release evidence show the requested behavior is implemented, but the issue was opened by a collaborator and frames a deliberate product/security namespace choice.

options.title: Accept shipped handle policy
options.body: Close this issue after confirming dot and underscore publisher handles are the intended ClawHub namespace model.

options.title: Keep open for alias policy
options.body: Leave this issue open only if maintainers want first-class scope-to-publisher aliases or slug-safe handles instead of the shipped behavior.

options.title: Reconsider shipped policy
options.body: Open a focused follow-up to change or revert the policy if npm-compatible handles create unacceptable URL or namespace tradeoffs.

recommendation.title: Accept shipped handle policy
recommendation.body: Close this issue after confirming dot and underscore publisher handles are the intended ClawHub namespace model.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the issue and the merged implementation and have the strongest recent history in this publisher/package policy area.
